title: Introduction to biofuels
author: Mousdale, David M.
summary: "What role will biofuels play in the scientific portfolio that might bring energy independence and security, revitalize rural infrastructures, and wean us off of our addiction to oil? The shifting energy landscape of the 21st century, with its increased demand for renewable energy technology, poses a worrying intellectual challenge. Discussing the multidisciplinary study of bioenergy and its potential for replacing fossil fuels in the coming decades, Introduction to Biofuels provides a roadmap for understanding the broad sweep of technological, sociological, and energy policy issues that intermingle and intertwine." "Copiously illustrated and with numerous examples, this book explores key technologies, including biotechnology, bioprocessing, and genetic reprogramming of microorganisms. The author examines the future of biofuels from a broader perspective, addressing the economic, social, and environmental issues crucial for studying the sustainable development of bioenergy. Each chapter begins with questions and provides the answers later in the chapter as key informational points. Embedded Science, Technology, Engineering, and Math (STEM) sections provide detailed derivations and equations for a subset of topics that can be found easily as buzzwords in popular media and on web sites. Together, the STEM topics form a thread of essential quantitative parameters that are crucial to the evergrowing biofuels database." "With so much information scattered throughout the literature, it is often difficult to make sense of what is real and what is an optimistic selling of ideas with no scientific credibility. This book does an excellent job of filtering through volumes of data, providing a historical perspective on which to anchor the information, and outlining the strenghts and constraints of the different biofuels."--BOOK JACKET.

title: 金門曆史建築導覽. 第二冊 | Jinmen li shi jian zhu dao lan. Di er ce
author: Huang, Zhenliang
summary: Kinmen has long placed great importance on clan culture, a tradition deeply rooted in Confucian values of filial piety. This form of social and familial organization has been highly respected by the people of Kinmen throughout history. The island is home to over 190 ancestral halls belonging to various family surnames, of which 11 have been officially designated as historic buildings. Additionally, there are 9 temples associated with Minnan folk religion, 1 Christian church, and 4 tombs, which are the burial sites of founding ancestors or locally renowned figures who made significant contributions. Due to its strategic role as a military outpost for over 40 years, Kinmen also preserves numerous military heritage sites, including bunkers, fortifications, and monuments. There are also educational institutions that were closely tied to the island's military functions—these military-education sites represent a unique blend of education and defense, reflecting Kinmen’s historical role. These architectural sites are considered some of Kinmen’s most valuable cultural assets, and this book primarily focuses on describing them. In cases where the owner of a building or their personal background had a particularly significant influence on the structure, the text begins with a brief analysis of the historical and social context, to help readers better understand the connection between the individual, the era, and the building itself
